chapter: Hollywood and the break with Thornhill
title: Victor session of June 1938 and 'St. Louis Blues'
summary: Titles of the June session and why 'St. Louis Blues' was timed with the film.

story.theme_name: Jazz musicians in the movies and film scoring
story.community_name: Jazz musicians on film and studio scoring

blocks.x: Now we come to the 29th of June 1938, when you recorded four sides for Victor again: 'Spring Is Here,' 'Down The Old Ox Road,' 'St. Louis Blues,' and 'L'amour Toujours L'Amour'.
Was there any significance to your singing 'St. Louis Blues' at this time and the slow coming appearance that you made in the movie?
Well, I think we sort of anticipated a little bit there, because it takes time for a record -- from the time you cut it until the time that it's released --
I had been called to go out to Hollywood.

They were getting ready to do the picture "St. Louis Blues."

I don't know why they called it the "St. Louis Blues" except for the fact they might've had a chance for the W. C. Handy folks to make some money on it; because up until that time, I think was the end of the 28-year period of the copyright can be (inaudible) renewed.
From what I could understand is, he hadn't really made -- received any royalties up until that time.
In fact, I think that ASCAP was founded around that same period we made the movie and the -- and, of course, my record naturally. They would royalties from that.
But naming the picture St. Louis Blues would give them a chance to get some rights for the title.
So, we figured will be released about the same time the recording will be released, and that will help both.
